title: Permissions
goal: Read a permission string, then tighten a secret and share a note on purpose.

cheatSheet.description: Read the mode. -rw-r--r-- is owner read/write, everyone else read.
Owner can read and write. Group and others have no access.
Owner can write. Everyone can read. A normal shared note.
Add execute for the owner only. This lab does not run the file.
Change the owner. Here you may give away a file you own, so you can see the result.

files.content:
API token for the lab dashboard: aterx-lab-demo-token
This is fake. Do not reuse it anywhere.
Tutor notes. The group should be able to read this.
Handover notes for the lab account.

tasks.prompt: Long-list the lab directory so you can read the modes.
tasks.hint: ls -l lab from home, or cd lab and then ls -l.

tasks.prompt: Change lab/secrets.txt so only the owner can read and write it.
tasks.hint: That mode is 600. chmod 600 takes the file path.

tasks.prompt: Read lab/secrets.txt and confirm you still can, now that you are the owner.
tasks.hint: chmod 600 does not lock the owner out. cat the file after the mode has changed.

tasks.prompt: Make lab/notes.txt readable by everyone, and still writable by the owner.
tasks.hint: 644 means rw-r--r--. The file starts out tighter than that.

tasks.prompt: Add owner execute on lab/collect.sh. Do not run the script.
tasks.hint: chmod u+x adds the bit for the owner. This lab never executes files.

tasks.prompt: Give lab/shared.txt to the lab user.
tasks.hint: chown lab takes the file next. On a real server only root can do this. This lab allows it so you can see ls -l change.
